title: DistributedComponentSmoothNonconvex.lean

problem_class.label: nonconvex
problem_class.details: Each component fᵢ has an Lᵢ-Lipschitz gradient, with Lᵢ ≥ 0. Components and their average may be nonconvex. The average F is bounded below by some a with F(x₀) − a ≤ Δ.

problem_class.label: finite_sum
problem_class.details: F(x) = (1/n)∑ᵢ fᵢ(x), with n ≥ 1 and one component per worker. The average (1/n)∑ᵢ Lᵢ bounds the smoothness of F.

oracle.label: stochastic_gradient
oracle.details: At every x, the jointly measurable oracle gᵢ satisfies E[gᵢ(x,ξ)] = ∇fᵢ(x). Each worker consumes consecutive fresh samples from its own IID stream with law μᵢ. The streams are independent across workers.

oracle.label: component_gradient
oracle.details: Worker i can query its own component fᵢ at a point x. A query specifies a positive batch size m and returns a list of m local gradient samples at x.
oracle.evidence: LongTails/Setups/DistributedComponentSmoothNonconvex.lean, spec.ComputeQuery and spec.admissible. LongTails/Setups/BandwidthHeterogeneousSmoothNonconvex.lean, ComputeQuery, ComputeReply and computation

distinctive_assumptions.label: bounded_variance
distinctive_assumptions.details: Each worker has its own public bound σᵢ ≥ 0. At every x, E‖gᵢ(x,ξ) − ∇fᵢ(x)‖² ≤ σᵢ². The bound concerns noise around the local component gradient.

distinctive_assumptions.label: finite_dimensional
distinctive_assumptions.details: The query and output space is Euclidean ℝᵈ, with public dimension d.
distinctive_assumptions.evidence: LongTails/Setups/DistributedComponentSmoothNonconvex.lean, Params.d, Point and spec.Output. LongTails/Setups/BandwidthHeterogeneousSmoothNonconvex.lean, Point. LongTails/Setups/DistributedSmoothNonconvex.lean, Point

distinctive_assumptions.label: other
distinctive_assumptions.details: A batch of m samples occupies worker i for m hᵢ time, with hᵢ > 0 and one pending batch per worker. Workers can compute concurrently with one another and with communication. Each ordered pair has its own FIFO link. Sending k payload bits takes l + b(k + 64) time once the link is available, with l,b ≥ 0. All setup parameters, including x₀, Δ, ε and the worker-specific hᵢ, Lᵢ, σᵢ, are public. The component functions, oracle maps and sampling laws are hidden.
distinctive_assumptions.evidence: LongTails/Setups/DistributedComponentSmoothNonconvex.lean, Params, spec.publicInput, spec.valid and spec.admissible. LongTails/Setups/BandwidthHeterogeneousSmoothNonconvex.lean, computation and communication. LongTails/TemplateDistributed.lean, Time, clockBits and step

accuracy.label: gradient_norm_squared
accuracy.details: The designated root returns a measurable point X by the stated elapsed-time deadline. The criterion uses the squared Euclidean norm of the gradient of the full average F at X.

accuracy.label: expected
accuracy.details: ‖∇F(X)‖² must be integrable and E‖∇F(X)‖² ≤ ε² for ε > 0. The expectation uses the product law of the algorithm seed and the oracle streams. The elapsed-time budget is fixed.
accuracy.evidence: LongTails/Setups/DistributedComponentSmoothNonconvex.lean, spec.valid and spec.successful. LongTails/TemplateDistributed.lean, law and TimedConvergence

setup_category.label: non_standard
setup_category.reason: The stationarity problem couples worker-specific smoothness and noise bounds with unequal sampling times and concurrent, bit-priced communication. Success is measured at a root worker under a fixed elapsed-time deadline.

descriptionHtml:
Distributed Nonconvex Finite-Sum Optimization

We seek a stationary point of a possibly nonconvex objective F on d-dimensional Euclidean space Rd. Each worker contributes one component to the average F. Each component has a Lipschitz gradient, and the initial objective gap to a global lower bound is bounded. Workers compute at heterogeneous speeds and communicate over directed links. Each worker’s oracle returns batches of unbiased local gradient estimates with bounded variance, using independent samples within and across workers. For a tolerance ε>0, the goal is an output x¯ satisfying E[∥∇F(x¯)∥2]≤ε2 over sampling and algorithm randomness.

Index the n≥1 workers by i=1,…,n, and write fi:Rd→R for their components, where d is a nonnegative integer. With F(x)=1n∑i=1nfi(x), the optimization problem is infx∈RdF(x). The algorithm receives d, n, the measurable sample space Ω, the starting point x0∈Rd, the bounds (Li,σi)i=1n and Δ, the tolerance ε, and the timing parameters (hi)i=1n, ℓ, and b.

Our assumptions:

Assumption 1 (Component smoothness and initial gap). Each fi is differentiable, and for all x,y∈Rd its gradient satisfies ∥∇fi(x)−∇fi(y)∥≤Li∥x−y∥,Li≥0, where ∥⋅∥ is the Euclidean norm. There is a lower bound a∈R such that a≤F(x)for every x∈Rd,F(x0)−a≤Δwith Δ≥0.

Assumption 2 (Local stochastic gradients). Worker i has a stream (ξi,k)k≥0 of measurable, independent samples with common law μi on Ω. The worker streams are mutually independent, and the algorithm’s randomness is independent of the entire sample array. The map gi:Rd×Ω→Rd is jointly measurable. For every x∈Rd and ξ∼μi, the vector gi(x,ξ) is Bochner integrable, its squared error is integrable, and Eξ∼μi[gi(x,ξ)]=∇fi(x),Eξ∼μi[∥gi(x,ξ)−∇fi(x)∥2]≤σi2, where σi≥0.

Computation and communication.

A computation query at worker i specifies a point x∈Rd and a positive integer batch size m. If k samples have already been used, the worker returns the ordered batch (gi(x,ξi,k+j))j=0m−1 after time mhi, where hi>0 is its time per sample. Each worker processes one batch at a time and ignores further computation requests while a batch is pending. Different workers can compute concurrently.

Every ordered pair of workers, including a worker paired with itself, has a directed link. A message with q≥0 payload bits is padded with 64 zero bits. If submitted at time t, it finishes at max{t,tprev}+ℓ+b(q+64), where tprev is the previous finish time on that link, initially zero, ℓ≥0 is the latency, and b≥0 is the time per transmitted bit. The recipient receives the sender’s identity and the padded bit string. Each link serves messages in submission order. Distinct links can operate concurrently, and communication can overlap computation.

Elapsed time and accuracy.

For an elapsed-time budget T≥0, almost surely the algorithm must process only finitely many events for every deadline s∈[0,T]. At time T, a root worker designated by the algorithm must produce a measurable output x¯∈Rd with integrable squared gradient norm satisfying E[∥∇F(x¯)∥2]≤ε2.

comparisonHtml:
On Rd, F=n−1∑ifi is bounded below, F(x0)−infF≤Δ, and ∇fi is Li-Lipschitz. Worker i has a jointly measurable unbiased gradient oracle with variance at most σi2. Samples are IID within workers and independent across workers. Workers compute in parallel, one batch per worker at a time, at hi>0 time per sample. Computation and communication can overlap. The complete multiport network serves each directed link in FIFO order. An m-bit message takes ℓ+bm time. Here n≥1, Li,σi,Δ,ℓ,b≥0, and ε>0. By the deadline, the execution returns a measurable X with Eexec∥∇F(X)∥2≤ε2 and almost surely completes only finitely many events.

import LongTails.Setups.BandwidthHeterogeneousSmoothNonconvex

namespace LongTails.Setups.DistributedComponentSmoothNonconvex

open MeasureTheory DistributedTemplate
open StochasticSmoothAndConvex (IsStochasticGradient)
open StochasticGeneralizedSmoothAndConvex (IID)

structure Params where
  d : ℕ
  n : ℕ+
  Ω : Type
  [measurableΩ : MeasurableSpace Ω]
  h : Fin n → Time
  l : Time
  b : Time
  L : Fin n → ℝ
  Δ : ℝ
  σ : Fin n → ℝ
  ε : ℝ
  x0 : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)

attribute [instance] Params.measurableΩ

noncomputable def smoothness (p : Params) : ℝ := (∑ i, p.L i) / p.n

noncomputable abbrev network (p : Params) : BandwidthHeterogeneousSmoothNonconvex.Params where
  d := p.d
  n := p.n
  Ω := p.Ω
  h := p.h
  l := p.l
  b := p.b
  L := smoothness p
  Δ := p.Δ
  σ := 0
  ε := p.ε
  x0 := p.x0

abbrev Point (p : Params) := BandwidthHeterogeneousSmoothNonconvex.Point (network p)
abbrev Functions (p : Params) := BandwidthHeterogeneousSmoothNonconvex.Functions (network p)
abbrev Samples (p : Params) := BandwidthHeterogeneousSmoothNonconvex.Samples (network p)

noncomputable def spec : Setup where
  Params := Params
  Public := Params
  numWorkers p := p.n
  Instance := Functions
  ComputeQuery p := BandwidthHeterogeneousSmoothNonconvex.ComputeQuery (network p)
  ComputeReply p := BandwidthHeterogeneousSmoothNonconvex.ComputeReply (network p)
  CommReply p := BandwidthHeterogeneousSmoothNonconvex.CommReply (network p)
  Output := Point
  publicInput := id
  valid p := (∀ i, 0 < p.h i) ∧ (∀ i, 0 ≤ p.L i) ∧ 0 ≤ p.Δ ∧ (∀ i, 0 ≤ p.σ i) ∧ 0 < p.ε
  admissible p f O :=
    let F := BandwidthHeterogeneousSmoothNonconvex.objective (network p) f
    (∀ i x, HasGradientAt (f i) (gradient (f i) x) x) ∧
    (∀ i x y, ‖gradient (f i) x - gradient (f i) y‖ ≤ p.L i * ‖x - y‖) ∧
    (∃ lower : ℝ, (∀ x, lower ≤ F x) ∧ F p.x0 - lower ≤ p.Δ) ∧
    ∃ (g : Fin p.n → Point p → p.Ω → Point p) (μ : Fin p.n → ProbabilityMeasure p.Ω)
      (P : ProbabilityMeasure (Samples p)),
      O = BandwidthHeterogeneousSmoothNonconvex.system (network p) g P ∧
      ProbabilityTheory.iIndepFun (fun i (s : Samples p) => s i) (P : Measure _) ∧
      ∀ i, IID (fun k (s : Samples p) => s i k) (μ i : Measure p.Ω) (P : Measure _) ∧
        IsStochasticGradient (Point p) p.Ω (μ i) (f i) (g i) (p.σ i)
  successful p f output P :=
    let F := BandwidthHeterogeneousSmoothNonconvex.objective (network p) f
    Measurable output ∧ Integrable (fun ω => ‖gradient F (output ω)‖ ^ 2) (P : Measure _) ∧
      (∫ ω, ‖gradient F (output ω)‖ ^ 2 ∂(P : Measure _)) ≤ p.ε ^ 2

end LongTails.Setups.DistributedComponentSmoothNonconvex
